explanation: Noodles aren't part of traditional Saudi cuisine, and no source documents a specific Saudi rule about slurping them. General Gulf dining etiquette favors restrained, quiet eating over loud table noises, so audible slurping would likely be seen as a minor lapse in manners rather than a serious offence.
local_tip: If eating noodles at a restaurant, favor quiet bites over loud slurping, since restrained table manners are generally valued.

also_check.note: Slurping noodles is read as a compliment to the chef and is expected in ramen shops.
Slurping is common and often read as enjoying the food.
Slurping pasta is considered a clear breach of table manners.

sources.title: Arab Table Manners: Business Lunch Etiquette in Arabic Countries
